claims.claim: Hook as seen by a viewer who swipes at second two: the Altar Stone was traced to Scotland in 2024 (A4).
claims.source_checked: Clarke 2024 full text https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07652-1?error=cookies_not_supported (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41586-024-07652-1; Clarke 2026 full text https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jqs.70080 (Firecrawl); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/jqs.70080; Pirrie 2026 full text https://www.lyellcollection.org/doi/full/10.1144/jgs2026-090 (Firecrawl); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1144/jgs2026-090
claims.note: A viewer leaving after the first sentence keeps 'traced to Scotland in 2024', which is true as a dated statement. The NE Scotland source is questioned (Pirrie 2026) but not refuted, and is still favoured by Clarke 2026 ('closest match in zircon age structure') and accepted by Parker Pearson 2024, so the early-swipe impression is not contradicted by any source. The second sentence states the dispute.

claims.claim: Two years on, scientists still can't agree where it came from.
claims.source_checked: Clarke 2026 full text https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jqs.70080 (Firecrawl); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/jqs.70080; Pirrie 2026 full text https://www.lyellcollection.org/doi/full/10.1144/jgs2026-090 (Firecrawl); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1144/jgs2026-090; Parker Pearson 2024 full-text PDF https://journals.uclpress.co.uk/ai/article/id/3293/download/pdf/ and landing page https://journals.uclpress.co.uk/ai/article/id/3293/ (via doi.org/10.14324/AI.27.1.13); Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.14324/AI.27.1.13
claims.note: Clarke 2026 (online 4 Jun 2026) still favours mainland NE Scotland (Caithness 'closest match') while 'its source location within this large basin remains unresolved'. Pirrie 2026 (online 5 Nov 2026): multi-proxy data 'raises questions over this interpretation'; chrome spinel scarcity 'may indicate that an origin from this part of NE Scotland needs re-evaluating'; clay mineralogy 'would exclude Caithness and Orkney'; Conclusions 'provenance ... has yet to be determined with confidence'. Parker Pearson 2024 p.129: 'the actual outcrop ... is unknown'. Aug 2024 to Nov 2026 is about two years. Disagreement is real and current.

Pirrie 2026 does not dispute the age match (a 'virtually identical age pattern' in Orcadian Basin ORS), only that it is unique; the samples are debitage 'confidently attributed' to the stone.
